name: Mawu-Lisa (Fon)

domain_history.domain: composite creator deity (Mawu: moon/night, female; Lisa: sun/day, male), generated by the withdrawn primordial figure Nana Buluku; head of the Dahomean state pantheon

notes: The Mawu-Lisa cult was imported from Aja territory and installed as head of the Dahomean state pantheon specifically by Hwanjile, the kpojito ("queen mother"/reign-mate) of King Tegbesu (r. c.1740-1774) — a documented act of religious-political legitimation tied to consolidating Tegbesu's contested succession, not a static inherited cosmology. Edna G. Bay, Wives of the Leopard: Gender, Politics, and Culture in the Kingdom of Dahomey (University of Virginia Press, 1998).
